# `silk/tls/server`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

A TLS 1.3 server state machine over byte buffers that you drive, with an ECDSA P-256
certificate.

## When to use
Use it to serve TLS from an event loop, such as the HTTPS mode of `silk.http.serve`. Load the
certificate chain and the private key one time with [`TlsServerConfig.fromPem`](#TlsServerConfig.impl.fromPem). Then make one
[`TlsServer`](#TlsServer) for each connection, pass received bytes to [`TlsServer.receive`](#TlsServer.impl.receive), and encrypt
application data with [`TlsServer.seal`](#TlsServer.impl.seal).

## Details
The server speaks TLS 1.3 only (RFC 8446), with the cipher suites TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256
and TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, the key exchange group X25519, and the signature algorithm
`ecdsa_secp256r1_sha256`. It picks ChaCha20-Poly1305 unless the client offers only AES-128-GCM.
When the client offers ALPN with `http/1.1`, the server selects it.

[`TlsServer.receive`](#TlsServer.impl.receive) consumes complete records from the input. It appends the records it
answers with to the output, and the decrypted application data to the plaintext list. It reads
a client `KeyUpdate` and answers a request for one. A `close_notify` alert sets the status to
`Closed`.

## Errors
- [`TlsConfigError`](#TlsConfigError) from [`TlsServerConfig.fromPem`](#TlsServerConfig.impl.fromPem) for a PEM text that it cannot use.
- A protocol error from the client makes [`TlsServer.receive`](#TlsServer.impl.receive) append an alert to the output and
  return the `Failed` status with the alert. The connection cannot be used after that.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if a buffer cannot grow.

## Gotchas
- No client certificates, session resumption, 0-RTT, or HelloRetryRequest: a client that sends
  no X25519 key share gets a `handshake_failure` alert.
- The server does not check its own certificate chain. Give the leaf certificate first.
- Secrets are not erased.

Import as `TlsServer` with `import silk.tls.server { TlsServer }`.

<a id="TlsServerConfig"></a>

## `TlsServerConfig`

```silk
pub struct TlsServerConfig
```

The certificate chain and the private key of a server.

### Details
The chain is kept as the body of a TLS `Certificate` message, ready to send. One config serves
every connection and every thread.

<a id="TlsServerConfig.impl"></a>

## Implementation `TlsServerConfig`

```silk
impl TlsServerConfig
```

<a id="TlsServerConfig.impl.fromPem"></a>

### Associated function `fromPem`

```silk
pub effect fn fromPem(certificates: &[u8], privateKey: &[u8]) -> TlsServerConfig
  ! TlsConfigError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads the certificate chain from the `CERTIFICATE` blocks of `certificates`, leaf first, and
the P-256 private key from the first `PRIVATE KEY` (PKCS #8) or `EC PRIVATE KEY` (SEC 1)
block of `privateKey`.

#### Errors
- `NoCertificate`, `InvalidPem`, `UnsupportedKey` or `ChainTooLarge` for input it cannot use.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the chain cannot be stored.

<a id="TlsServer.impl.receive"></a>

### Method `receive`

```silk
pub effect fn receive(
    self: &mut Self,
    config: &TlsServerConfig,
    input: &mut [u8],
    output: &mut List<u8>,
    plaintext: &mut List<u8>,
  ) -> TlsProgress ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Consumes the complete records at the start of `input`.

#### Details
It appends its answers, such as the server handshake flight, to `output`, and the decrypted
application data to `plaintext`. It decrypts in place, so it changes `input`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if a buffer cannot grow. Protocol errors are a `Failed` status.

<a id="TlsServer.impl.seal"></a>

### Method `seal`

```silk
pub effect fn seal(self: &mut Self, data: &[u8], output: &mut List<u8>) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Encrypts `data` as application data records, and appends them to `output`.

#### Details
Each record holds at most 16 KiB. Nothing is sent before the handshake is finished.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if `output` cannot grow.


<a id="TlsProtocol"></a>

## `TlsProtocol`

```silk
pub struct TlsProtocol<P>
```

A `silk.net.tcp_server` protocol that serves TLS 1.3 and runs `inner` over the decrypted bytes.

### Details
For each connection it makes a [`TlsServer`](#TlsServer) and the state of `inner`. Bytes that arrive are
decrypted and given to `inner`, and what `inner` writes is encrypted. When `inner` closes the
connection, the server sends `close_notify` first.
